questionText:
You are in Spain staying with your friend Juan. The two of you are making plans. Complete in SPANISH your side of the following DIALOGUE.
Juan: ¿Qué te gustaría hacer?
Tú: Say that you love sports and are a member of a gym in your town. Ask Juan if there is a sports centre nearby.
Juan: Bueno, hay uno en el hotel grande que se encuentra en la Plaza Mayor.
Tú: Tell him that you will go tomorrow to find out how much it costs. You hope that it is not too expensive. Explain that you couldn’t find a summer job because there is fifteen per cent unemployment in Ireland.
Juan: Aún peor aquí. Por eso no tengo mucho dinero y no podré salir mucho.
Tú: Tell Juan that you are tired after your journey and you would like to go to bed straight away. The flight from Cork was delayed due to fog.
Juan: Bueno. ¿Mañana te gustaría conocer a mis amigos? Podemos quedar con ellos por la tarde.
Tú: Suggest that perhaps you could all play basketball on the court at the end of the street. You would like to get to know them. Another day we could download a film to watch in the evening.
Juan: Mañana, entonces. La mayoría de mis amigos no habla muy bien el inglés. Tendrás que hablar en castellano.
Tú: Say that’s great. It will help you improve your spoken Spanish. Tell him your teacher loves grammar but that you never get a chance to speak the language with Spaniards.

questionText:
You have arrived in Spain and want to get a summer job. You go to the Hotel Artetxe in Bilbao and speak to the manager. Complete in SPANISH your side of the following DIALOGUE.
Directora: ¿En qué puedo ayudarle?
Tú: Introduce yourself. Say that you are Irish and have just arrived in Spain. Say you are looking for a part-time job until the first of October.
Directora: ¿Pues, tiene usted alguna experiencia?
Tú: Say that you worked in a youth hostel. You had to serve breakfast and clear the tables. Sometimes you also had to answer the phone and take messages.
Directora: Y, ¿habla usted muy bien el castellano?
Tú: Say that you have been studying Spanish for five years and find it easy. You speak English, of course, and understand a little French.
Directora: ¡Muy bien! Mucha gente viene aquí del sur de Francia. Lo que puedo ofrecerle de momento es un trabajo los fines de semana en el restaurante.
Tú: Say you can’t believe it! Work as a waiter/waitress is perfect for you. You are here on a scholarship and have to attend class from Monday to Friday.
Directora: Lo malo es que las horas son largas. Hay que trabajar hasta las dos o tres de la madrugada.
Tú: Say you don’t think that is a problem. Say that your friend can lend you a bicycle to get to and from work. Thank her for the job and ask how much you would be paid if you worked for 12 hours.

questionText:
Your Spanish friend, Laura, is on holidays in Ireland. Write a letter/e-mail to her in Spanish. Use all of the points mentioned below:
- Offer to take her to the city centre on Saturday afternoon.
- Tell her why you like going there.
- Tell her about your friends – who they are and what they are like.
- Say that later you will all go for lunch.
- Ask her if she would like to go to the cinema in the evening.

taskRequirements: There are five ‘messages’ to be communicated.
Allow a maximum of 8 marks for each of these.
(0 – 8 marks may be awarded for each message.)
8 marks x 5 = 40 marks
Full message unequivocally conveyed: 8 marks
Communication satisfactory: 6 marks
Communication adequate: 5 marks
Message comprehensible/ some details missing: 4 marks
Possible to extract some sense: 2 marks
rubric.markingGuideNote:
Candidates must attempt:
1. LETTER/E-MAIL and either 2. (a) MESSAGE or 2. (b)DIARY ENTRY.
practiceNotes: Write your answer in Spanish, then place it on the published grid. You are marked on this task alone, and where it asks you to choose statements, turns or points, on the ones you chose.

questionText:
You are attending a language course in Alicante. You ask to speak to Juan, the Principal of the school. Complete in SPANISH your side of the following DIALOGUE.
Juan: ¿Cómo te va todo?
Tú: Explain that you are not very happy. Your host family live a long way from the language school and you have to get a bus and then walk for fifteen minutes to arrive at nine o’ clock.
Juan: Bueno, la única solución es levantarte más temprano. ¿Qué tal con la familia?
Tú: Tell him that you get on well with the daughter. She is very friendly and helps you a lot with your Spanish. However, your room is very small and there is no wardrobe.
Juan: ¡Qué lástima! Y ¿qué te parece la comida en casa?
Tú: Explain that you are a vegetarian and the family eats a lot of meat and fish. You would like to eat salads and vegetables or maybe a Spanish omelette. The only things you can find to eat in the house are peaches and grapes.
Juan: Bueno, es que aquí en España se come mucha carne y pescado. ¿Pero, estás a gusto en las clases?
Tú: Explain that most of your classes are very good and your Spanish has improved a lot. The grammar is very difficult but the culture classes are fascinating, in particular the Spanish film class.
Juan: Pues, mañana por la tarde vamos a ir al cine con la clase.
Tú: Say that’s great. Tell him you are looking forward to going out with your class and would also like to get to know new people. Say that you often go to the cinema in Ireland.

questionText:

Communication adequate: 5 marks

Possible to extract some sense 2 marks

questionText:
You have arrived in Madrid to stay with the Martínez family for a month. You have just met the family at the airport. Complete in SPANISH your side of the following DIALOGUE. Sra. Martínez: Hola, bienvenido a España.
Tú: Say that you are delighted to meet them. Tell them that you have never been to Spain before and this is your first time away without your family. Sra. Martínez: Pero hablas muy bien el castellano.
Tú: Tell them you have been learning Spanish for five years and it is your favourite subject. However you hope it will improve while you are here as you need to get high marks in your Leaving Cert. Sra. Martínez: Pues aquí vas a conocer a muchos españoles.
Tú: That’s fantastic. Tell them you have heard that Spanish people are very friendly. Tell them you are a little worried about the weather as you don’t really like the heat. Sra. Martínez: No te preocupes. En casa tenemos aire acondicionado. Además, dentro de dos semanas vamos a ir todos a nuestra casa de verano en la costa.
Tú: Tell them you love water sports and swimming. Ask if it is possible to do a sailing course when you are by the sea. It would also be a great opportunity to practise your Spanish. Sra. Martínez: Creo que sí. Normalmente, ¿qué haces durante el verano?
Tú: Say that in Ireland you usually have to work. Your parents own a sports shop. You don’t mind because the customers are nice. However it will be good to relax for a month.

questionText:
You read an article in a Spanish newspaper about the negative effects part-time jobs have on the education of young people. You decide to write a LETTER/EMAIL in SPANISH to the editor of the newspaper.
(You may loosely base your letter/email on the points mentioned below, either agreeing or disagreeing with all or some of them. You should make five relevant points and each of these points should be expanded and developed.)
• Part-time jobs have many advantages.
• Young people need to learn to save money.
• Work experience is very useful for the future.
• Parents can’t be expected to fund their children all the time.
• Most young people can combine work and study.

questionText:
You have just received a letter from your Spanish friend, Juan. Write a letter/e-mail to him in Spanish. Use all of the points mentioned below:
- Say your exams finished last week and say how you feel.
- Explain how you celebrated.
- Say you are going to work in your uncle’s shop in July.
- Mention how you plan to spend the money you earn.
- Ask him if he would like to come to Ireland in August.

taskRequirements: There are five points to be communicated.
Allow a maximum of 8 marks for each of these.
(0 – 8 marks may be awarded for each detail.)
8 marks x 5 = 40 marks
Full message unequivocally conveyed: 8 marks
Communication satisfactory: 6 marks
Communication adequate: 5 marks
Message comprehensible / some details missing: 4 marks
Possible to extract some sense 2 marks
rubric.markingGuideNote:
Candidates must attempt:
1. LETTER/E-MAIL and either 2(a) NOTE or 2(b) DIARY ENTRY.

questionText:
You are working as an au pair in Santander. You go to the tourist office on the first morning to ask what activities there are for young people. Complete in SPANISH your side of the following DIALOGUE.
Juan: ¿En qué puedo ayudarle?
Tú: Explain that you arrived in Santander two days ago. You only work in the mornings so would like to know what there is for young people to do in Santander.
Juan: Bueno, ¿qué tipo de actividades le interesan?
Tú: Tell him that you are quite sporty and like outdoor activities but are also interested in Spanish culture. In particular, you hope to meet people of your own age.
Juan: Y, ¿qué le parece un campamento de deporte o clases de cocina?
Tú: Explain that you play for your local tennis club. Tell him you would love to cook some typical dishes for your family when you return home as they have never been to Spain.
Juan: Bueno, aquí en Santander hay muchas clases para usted. Otra cosa, debe visitar los Picos de Europa.
Tú: Brilliant! Say that you want to go hiking as you are near the mountains. You doubt if it’s possible to go this weekend but maybe later this month. Ask for a list of accommodation and a bus timetable.
Juan: Pues, aquí tiene un folleto con toda la información que necesita.
Tú: Thank Juan very much and tell him that you will ring a hostel this afternoon. Tell him that you are going to the shopping center straight away to buy runners and a raincoat.

questionText:
You have returned to Ireland after three weeks on a student exchange in Valencia. You meet your Spanish friend Juan. Complete in SPANISH your side of the following DIALOGUE.
Juan: ¿Qué tal te ha ido?
Tú: Explain that you arrived home late last night. You are still very tired as the flight was delayed and your bags are still in Spain.
Juan: ¿Qué te ha parecido Valencia?
Tú: Tell him that you really enjoyed your stay with your exchange student Esteban. Valencia has fantastic buildings and beautiful public parks. You love the Spanish way of life.
Juan: ¿Por qué te gusta tanto?
Tú: There is a great atmosphere in the city centre because the streets are always full of people. The food is very tasty, in particular the fresh fruit and the seafood paella.
Juan: ¿Tuviste la oportunidad de asistir al instituto con Esteban?
Tú: Yes. Explain that you liked the school because there are more subjects and every class lasts an hour. However, they do very little sport. It’s a disaster!
Juan: Pues, fue una buena experiencia para ti, ¿no?
Tú: Definitely. If you had the money you would return again next year. You would like to improve your Spanish as your dream is to work in a Spanish‐speaking country in the future.

questionText:
Your Spanish friend María lives in the city of Toledo, where you visited her last Easter. Write a letter / e‐mail to her in Spanish. Use all of the points mentioned below:
‐ Thank her for the great holiday in April.
‐ Say two things you like about Toledo.
‐ Say that you loved the Spanish sunshine and describe the weather in Ireland.
‐ Explain that your exams finished last week and say how you are going to celebrate.
‐ Say that you want to find a job for the summer and why you need one.

taskRequirements: There are five points to be communicated.
Allow a maximum of 8 marks for each of these.
(0 – 8 marks may be awarded for each point.)
8 marks x 5 = 40 marks
Full message unequivocally conveyed: (8m)
Communication satisfactory: (6m)
Communication adequate: (5m)
Message comprehensible / some details missing: (4m)
Possible to extract some sense (2m)

questionText:
You are on holidays in Malaga with your family. You go into a car hire office. Complete in SPANISH your side of the following DIALOGUE. Sr. García: Buenos días. ¿Qué desea?
Tú: Say that you are here on holidays with your parents and sister. Say that you want to rent a car for five days. Your parents are architects and would like to do a trip around Andalucia and its main cities. Sr. García: Pues, tienen que visitar Córdoba y Granada. Son ciudades fantásticas con unos edificios impresionantes.
Tú: Tell him that every summer your family visits a European country to explore the culture. Your mother will be driving. You have brought her driving licence, passport and credit card with you. Sr. García: Y, ¿qué tipo de coche necesita?
Tú: Something suitable for five people. You will need enough space for one suitcase and three backpacks, not to mention the amount of stuff your sister will buy. Sr. García: Bueno, tenemos un Seat a sesenta euros al día. Su madre tendría que venir aquí personalmente.
Tú: That seems a good price. At the moment your mother is on the balcony relaxing with a good book. You can all come back after lunch around two. Sr. García: La oficina está cerrada durante la siesta. ¿Pueden venir a las cinco?
Tú: No problem. Say that you will be here at exactly five o’clock to collect the car. You and your mother have to go to the airport to meet your grandmother who will be staying here for the next five days.

questionText:
You have just returned from a holiday with your Spanish friend, Pablo, who lives in Cadiz. Write a letter /e‐mail to him in Spanish. Use all of the points mentioned below:
‐ Say you had a great time in Cadiz last month.
‐ Tell him it will be your birthday next week and say how you will celebrate it.
‐ Explain that your parents are going to buy you a ticket for a concert.
‐ Invite Pablo to come to Ireland for two weeks in July.
‐ Suggest two things you can do during his visit.

taskRequirements: There are five points to be communicated.
Allow a maximum of 8 marks for each of these.
(0 – 8 marks may be awarded for each point.)
8 marks x 5 = 40 marks
Full message unequivocally conveyed: 8 marks
Communication satisfactory: 6 marks
Communication adequate: 5 marks
Message comprehensible / some details missing: 4 marks
Possible to extract some sense: 2 marks

1. LETTER / E-MAIL and either 2. (a) NOTE or 2 (b) DIARY ENTRY.

questionText:
You are in Huelva and you go to a shop to return an item you have bought. Complete in SPANISH your side of the following DIALOGUE.
Pilar: ¿En qué puedo ayudarte?
Tú: Explain that you bought a present for your mother here yesterday, a grey jacket. However, when you returned to your apartment you realized that it was too big.
Pilar: Bueno. ¿Quieres devolverla?
Tú: Yes, here it is. Tell her that you would like the same jacket but in size forty. Tell her this is your mother’s favourite shop in Spain.
Pilar: ¿Estás aquí de vacaciones?
Tú: Tell her you are here with a group of friends. You have just finished your exams and are spending a week here. You visited the city last year with your family.
Pilar: ¿Y qué es lo que más te gusta de Huelva?
Tú: Explain that you love the weather, of course, as it is much better than in Ireland. The people are also very friendly, like the Irish.
Pilar: Entonces, ¿te gustaría vivir aquí?
Tú: Your parents want you to go to university in Ireland. You would prefer to spend a year in Huelva first to improve your Spanish because you want to study languages in the future.

questionText:
You are planning to go to Spain after the exams. Your Spanish friend Enrique lives in Malaga. Write a letter / e-mail to him in Spanish. Use all of the points mentioned below:
- Tell him you don’t have much free time because you have to study for your exams.

questionText:
You have just arrived at the youth hostel. Complete in Spanish the dialogue. You should answer any five of the following points:
Raquel: Buenos días, ¿en qué puedo ayudarte?
Tú: Introduce yourself and say that you have just arrived in San Sebastián. Tell her that you booked a room for three nights on the hostel’s website.
Raquel: Perfecto, ya la veo. ¿Qué vas a hacer aquí?
Tú: Explain that you are going to spend two months here. You are doing a Spanish language course in the university.
Raquel: Y, ¿dónde vas a alojarte después de aquí?
Tú: Say that you want to share an apartment with some Spanish students to improve your Spanish. You are here alone and you don’t know anybody.
Raquel: Sí, me parece muy buena idea. ¿Por qué decidiste venir a San Sebastián?
Tú: Say that your friends have gone to the south of Spain to learn Spanish. You decided to come here because you prefer the climate in the north.
Raquel: La verdad es que es una ciudad muy bonita. ¿Qué sabes de San Sebastián?
Tú: Tell her that you love Spanish food and that San Sebastián is famous for its tapas. Say that you would love to try some of the typical dishes.
Raquel: No olvides que también hay playas magníficas y que el casco viejo está muy animado siempre.
Tú: Say that you are looking forward to visiting all the places of interest in the city. Of course you would like to make new friends also.

questionText:
You and your family are going to visit your cousins in Wexford. Write a letter / email in Spanish, to your friend María, who lives in Toledo. Use any five of the points mentioned below:
‐ Tell María you are going to spend a week with your cousins in Wexford.
‐ Describe the area where your cousins live.
‐ Say what you plan to do there.
‐ Describe one of your cousins.
‐ Say what the weather is like there in summer.
‐ Say what you did last summer.
‐ Ask María what she likes to do during the summer holidays.
‐ Give regards to her family, especially her sister Carmen.

taskRequirements: There are five points to be communicated. Allow a maximum of 8 marks for each of these.
(0 – 8 marks may be awarded for each point.) If more than five points are answered, mark all and award the marks for the five highest scoring points.
(5 x 8m = 40 marks)
Communicative intention fulfilled.
Good level of vocabulary. Verb(s) correct. 7 - 8 marks
Communicative intention more or less fulfilled.
Quite good level of vocabulary. Verb(s) generally correct. 5 - 6 marks
Some communicative intention fulfilled.
There may be a few errors. 3 - 4 marks
Possible to extract some communicative intention. 1 -2 marks
No communicative intention fulfilled. 0 marks
rubric.markingGuideNote:
All answers must be in Spanish.
Candidates must attempt:
1. LETTER / E-MAIL and either 2. (a) NOTE or 2 (b) DIARY ENTRY.

questionText:
You are going to a summer camp in Malaga to improve your Spanish. Complete in Spanish the following dialogue. You should attempt any five of the following points:
Señora López: Hola, ¿piensas venir a nuestro campamento de verano?
Tú: Say you think it would be ideal for you because the facilities are excellent. You have heard that the classes are not just fun but educational also.
Señora López: Pues, ¡eso depende del profesor! ¿Has ido antes a un campamento?
Tú: Say that when you were younger, you did various sports camps in Ireland during the summer holidays. Your favourite was the tennis camp.
Señora López: ¿Eres deportista? Porque aquí se pueden practicar muchos deportes.
Tú: Tell her that you love sport and it is very important in your life. In fact, you are captain of your school basketball team this year.
Señora López: Hablas español bastante bien.
Tú: Say that you have been studying Spanish for five years. Until now you have never had the opportunity to practise with Spanish people.
Señora López: Pues aquí no está permitido hablar inglés en los campamentos.
Tú: Say you understand, it seems a good idea. You spent two weeks in Connemara learning Irish one summer and they had the same rule there.
Señora López: Bueno, pienso que este campamento será perfecto para ti.
Tú: Thank Señora Lopez. Tell her that you will arrive in Malaga at the end of June, after finishing your exams and you will stay for two weeks.

questionText:
You are spending a year in Madrid and you want to join a local basketball club. Complete in Spanish the dialogue. You should attempt any five of the following points:
Entrenador: Buenos días, ¿así que quieres jugar al baloncesto con nosotros?
Tú: Say that you are delighted to meet him. Say that you are going to spend a year studying in Madrid and that you would like to stay fit.
Entrenador: Estupendo. ¿Juegas bien al baloncesto?
Tú: Say that you have never played basketball, you prefer Gaelic football. There was a good team in your school and they won the final last year.
Entrenador: Si, conozco el fútbol gaélico. ¡Los mejores jugadores deben ser muy ricos!
Tú: Say that they don’t earn anything, they love the sport. The GAA is a voluntary organisation and a very important part of Irish culture.
Entrenador: ¿No eres un poco bajito/a para jugar al baloncesto?
Tú: Say that’s true, you are not very tall, but you are smart. You don’t mind training often and you get on well with your team mates.
Entrenador: Pues, entrenamos los martes y los jueves a las siete de la tarde.
Tú: Tell him that seems ok, but you will arrive a bit late as your classes in the university don’t finish until six thirty every day.
Entrenador: No te preocupes. ¿Te puedo ayudar en algo más?
Tú: Say that your parents love basketball and you want to bring them to a game during their visit in January. Ask is it difficult to get tickets.

questionText:
You have just arrived in Murcia, where you meet your new Spanish flat-mate, Gabriela. Complete in Spanish the following dialogue. You should attempt any five of the following six points:
Gabriela: ¡Bienvenido/a a Murcia! ¿Qué tal el viaje?
Tú: Say that it was a long journey because you had to get up very early to get a bus to Dublin airport. Then your flight was delayed because of the bad weather.
Gabriela: Ay, ¡qué mala suerte! ¿Dónde están tus maletas?
Tú: Tell her that you only have your rucksack, as your suitcase didn’t arrive from Dublin. The airline is looking for it and they are going to call you when they find it.
Gabriela: A mí me ha pasado varias veces. Las aerolíneas son un desastre.
Tú: Say that she is right, the worst thing is that you have no summer clothes and you need to go shopping. Ask if there is a shopping centre nearby.
Gabriela: Sí, hay un Corte Inglés a la vuelta de la esquina, y hay muchas tiendas por aquí. ¿Has conocido al dueño del apartamento?
Tú: Say that you have rented the apartment through an agency, you spoke with the owner on Whatsapp. He told you that there are two other people living here.
Gabriela: Sí, los otros se llaman Adrián y Patricia. Los dos son españoles y son muy sociables.
Tú: Say you are looking forward to meeting them. You understand a lot of Spanish and you watch some Spanish TV but at times you find it difficult to speak the language.
Gabriela: Normal, pues aquí tendrás muchas oportunidades de practicar.
Tú: Ask her if she would like to go for something to eat with you. Say that you are really hungry and you would love to explore the area and try typical dishes.

• Ireland is an expensive country to visit.
• There are lots of historic sites to see.
• Irish music and traditions are famous worldwide.
• The climate is not extreme.
• There are many flights from Spain to Ireland.
• Ireland is a small country, so it is easy to travel around.
• Ireland produces good food.
• Irish people are very friendly.

questionText:
You are talking to your Spanish friend Jorge about his plans to study abroad next year. Complete in Spanish the following dialogue. You should attempt any five of the following points:
Jorge: He conseguido una beca Erasmus para pasar un curso académico en una universidad extranjera el año que viene. ¡Qué ilusión!
Tú: Tell him that’s great news, you are delighted because the process to go on Erasmus is very long and difficult, especially the personal essay and the interview.
Jorge: Pues sí, estoy muy contento, y ¡mi familia está muy orgullosa!
Tú: Say that your sister did Erasmus in Austria three years ago, she enjoyed the experience and made friends from different countries. Ask him where he’s planning to study.
Jorge: Pues, no sé. La beca me permite elegir cualquier país de la Comunidad Europea.
Tú: You would love to go to Spain because it has such a rich culture. You’ve heard that Salamanca is one of the oldest universities in the world.
Jorge: ¡No lo sabía! En este momento estoy pensando en Francia o Irlanda.
Tú: Say that without doubt France has many advantages. The language is similar to Spanish, the universities offer a variety of courses and it is also close to Spain.
Jorge: Exactamente. Por ejemplo, si estuviera en Burdeos podría volver a Bilbao en tren algunos fines de semana.
Tú: Say that Ireland is a good option too. Outside Dublin it is not as expensive as France, but it can be difficult to find somewhere to live.
Jorge: Gracias por los consejos, no tengo que tomar una decisión hasta el mes que viene.
Tú: Ask him if he would like to go out at the weekend to celebrate. Say there is a concert in the stadium on Saturday and many of your friends are going to be there.

questionText:

‐ Tell him you are very tired because you are studying for your exams.
‐ Say what you did to celebrate your birthday last weekend.
‐ Mention two things you like about school.
‐ Tell him about your part‐time job.
‐ Describe how you will get to Santander.
‐ Mention what you would like to do in Santander.
‐ Give him your opinion on Spanish food.
‐ Tell him about your plans for the rest of the summer.

You are staying in Palma de Mallorca with your Spanish friend, Sara. Leave her a note, in Spanish, including any four of the following points:
‐ Say you are going to the city centre by bus.
‐ Tell her you are going shopping.
‐ Ask if she would like to go to the cinema with you at 8pm.
‐ Say you will go for tapas later.
‐ Tell her you will not be home for dinner.

taskRequirements: Identical allocation in each case.
There are four points to be communicated. Allow a maximum of 5 marks for each of these.
(0 to 5 marks may be awarded for each point.) If more than four points are answered, mark all and award the marks for the four highest scoring points.
(4 x 5m = 20 marks)
Message fully conveyed, no grammatical errors. 5 marks
Message more or less conveyed, some grammatical errors. 4 marks
Message partly comprehensible. 3 marks
Possible to extract some sense of message. 2 marks
Very small amount of message conveyed. 1 mark
No communication of message. 0 marks
rubric.markingGuideNote:
All answers must be in Spanish.
Candidates must attempt:
1. LETTER / E‐MAIL and either 2. (a) NOTE or 2 (b) DIARY ENTRY.
practiceNotes: Write your answer in Spanish, then place it on the published grid. You are marked on this task alone, and where it asks you to choose statements, turns or points, on the ones you chose.

questionText:
You are interested in doing volunteer work for the summer. You go to an organisation in Madrid. Complete in Spanish the dialogue. You should attempt any five of the following points:
Begoña: Buenos días, ¿qué tal el viaje?
Tú: Say that it was complicated because your apartment is on the other side of the city. You are not used to a lot of traffic as you are from a small town in Ireland.
Begoña: Sí, los atascos son terribles. Así que ¿quieres hacer un voluntariado con nuestra ONG?
Tú: Say that you are interested in working in Latin America. Your brother took part in a project in Argentina last summer and said it was an unforgettable experience.
Begoña: Tenemos proyectos en Argentina, México y Perú. ¿Cuál sería tu opción preferida?
Tú: You would prefer to work in Argentina. Some of your friends are from there and you would love to meet up with them at the end of the summer.
Begoña: Argentina es preciosa. ¿Has traído una copia de tu currículum?
Tú: Tell her that you are sorry, you don’t have it with you. You sent a copy by email to her colleague Rosa a week ago, but she did not answer.
Begoña: Ahora lo veo. Háblame de tu experiencia laboral.
Tú: Say that your uncle works in construction and you worked with him last summer. Say that you are hardworking and you get on well with everybody.
Begoña: Estupendo, creo que podrías ser valioso/a para nuestro equipo en Argentina.
Tú: Thank her for her time. Say that you will ring your friend Pablo in Buenos Aires to tell him the good news when you return home.

questionText:
Your Spanish friend Miguel is coming to visit you in July. Write a letter/e-mail to him in Spanish. Use any five of the points mentioned below:
- Describe the area where you live.
- Say what the weather is like in Ireland in summer.
- Ask him if he would he like to go to Dublin with you.
- Say what you could do in Dublin.
- Tell Miguel you have exams in June.
- Say that you are going on holidays after the exams.
- Tell him you are going to work in a restaurant in August.
- Mention your plans for next year.

taskRequirements: There are five points to be communicated. Allow a maximum of 8 marks for each of these.
(0 – 8 marks may be awarded for each point). If more than five points are answered, mark all and award the marks for the five highest scoring points.
(5 x 8m = 40 marks)
Communicative intention fulfilled.
Good level of vocabulary. Verb(s) correct. 7 - 8 marks
Communicative intention more or less fulfilled.
Quite good level of vocabulary. Verb(s) generally correct. 5 - 6 marks
Some communicative intention fulfilled.
There may be a few errors. 3 - 4 marks
Possible to extract some communicative intention. 1 -2 marks
No communicative intention fulfilled. 0 marks
rubric.markingGuideNote:
All answers must be in Spanish.
Candidates must attempt:
1. LETTER / E-MAIL and either 2. (a) NOTE or 2 (b) DIARY ENTRY.
practiceNotes: Write your answer in Spanish, then place it on the published grid. You are marked on this task alone, and where it asks you to choose statements, turns or points, on the ones you chose.
Mark each point you wrote on its own against the scheme's ladder above.
